questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Nauru?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nauru article.

questions.proof: English and Nauruan are the official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “With 10,670 residents, it is the third least-populated country after Vatican City and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “City”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nauru article.

questions.proof: With 10,670 residents, it is the third least-populated country after Vatican City and Tuvalu.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Its nearest neighbour is _____, 300 kilometres (190 mi) east.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “neighbour”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nauru article.

questions.proof: Its nearest neighbour is Kiribati, 300 kilometres (190 mi) east.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Nauru is a phosphate rock island, and its main export since _____ has been phosphate.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nauru article.

questions.proof: Nauru is a phosphate rock island, and its main export since 1907 has been phosphate.
